Markus / all —

Quick diagnostics: our telemetry shows KV cache thrash and connection queue saturation in westus2 AZ1 starting ~07:26. There are concurrent host-level GC events on a subset of instances and a spike in inter-AZ network retransmits. Impact: request tail latency and error amplification on long-tail requests — matches FinServe metrics.

Recommended immediate actions (short timeline):
- Activate geo-evacuation: steer 80% of FinServe traffic to uswest1 (health-checked variant) using weighted routing (5m rollout).
- Spin up emergency Dedicated capacity (quantized GPU pool) in uswest1 with auto-attach for FinServe; pre-warm KV caches from last known prefix to reduce cold misses.
- Enable prefix-level caching for the most common payment paths and reduce max-inflight per-connection to limit retries.

Rollback plan: if error rate in uswest1 >2% after 10m, revert to original routing and throttle FinServe to degrade gracefully (5QPS cap per shard).

Attachments: evac_playbook_v2.pdf (ops playbook excerpt)

I'll start the routing change the moment I have exec sign-off. Need operations window for pre-warm ~6–8 minutes.

—Hannah
Director, Site Reliability

+1 to Hannah's plan. Technical notes on execution:
- I'll open REQ-4492 to request immediate capacity allocation in uswest1 and set priority to emergency. We can request a 1-hour reserved pool for FinServe and bill to emergency account.
- Routing changes: we'll push a canary at 20% -> 50% -> 80% over 5m windows with active probe gating. I'll instrument synthetic health checks and add a trace header so we can correlate errors end-to-end.
- Estimated cost impact: ~$4.2k/hr for the dedicated pre-warm pool while active; secondary egress and cross-region traffic ~+12% for the duration.

I'll prepare the rollback triggers and telemetry dashboards; will ping once REQ is accepted and capacity is live.

—Rishi
